title: Quarterly access recertification — field notes and SIEM mapping (Q2 2026)
content:
Purpose:
These are field notes from the Q2 2026 least-privilege recertification window for privileged and sensitive roles. This doc captures operational observations, SIEM export mappings used for evidence automation, gaps encountered with RBAC v2 role derivation, and a short remediation backlog. Use this as the ground-truth for the post-mortem and for improving the orchestration runbook.

Scope and targets:
- Scope: all identities flagged as 'privileged' or 'sensitive' in the entitlement catalog (svc-accounts, admin roles, infra operators, release-engineering deploy roles).
- Samples: 1,942 unique principals evaluated during the 10-day window (May 1–10, 2026).
- Exclusions: short-lived CI tokens auto-rotated every 6 hours (handled by CI policy) and third-party vendor accounts with separate attestation process (legal approved).

High-level outcome summary:
- 1,318 principals retained with no change.
- 324 principals had role reductions (removed admin-level entitlements).
- 89 principals were disabled or scheduled for deprovisioning (stale service accounts / unowned human accounts).
- 211 exception requests were opened; 43 were approved as temporary exceptions (30–90 days).

What worked (observations):
- SIEM export pipeline (Kinesis -> SIEM -> evidence-bucket) reliably provided activity windows for ~94% of principals. Exports included: auth_success, auth_failed, role_grant, role_revoke, token_create, token_expire.
- Evidence automation (evidence-generator lambda) successfully attached audit fragments (last 90 days) to 1,760 recertification tickets.
- RBAC v2 derived-role mapping correctly flattened legacy role tags for 86% of evaluated principals; the remaining mismatches correlated with older role_bindings that had embedded project-prefixed names.
- A/B rollout of 'limited-review' policy (auto-approve non-privileged read-only entitlements) reduced reviewer workload by ~18% for infra-read roles.

Gaps and root causes identified:
1) Incomplete audit log schema coverage for 'service-account-impersonation' events. Several automation flows impersonate service accounts via the token exchange API; these events were not consistently marked as impersonation in the audit schema (missing impersonator_id field). Impact: inability to prove delegated action lineage for ~76 principals.
2) Timezone drift in SIEM ingestion caused 2–3 hour windows of missing activity for logs from APAC regions on May 3rd. Root cause: the forwarder container's TZ env was overridden during a sidecar update.
3) RBAC v2 role derivation: legacy role_bindings with custom attributes (role:deploy:project-*) were not normalized by the mapping script. Resulted in duplicate derived-roles and false-positive entitlements.
4) Evidence attachments: some large audit fragments (>>5MB) were rejected by the ticketing system (size limit). We ended up attaching summary artifacts only, decreasing evidence fidelity.

Temporary mitigations we used during the run:
- Manual tagging of impersonation events: security ops appended an 'impersonation=true' label in the SIEM for affected principals and regenerated attachments.
- Local time correction: restarted forwarder containers with TZ env set to UTC and backfilled missing logs from cold-s3 storage.
- Role normalization hotfix: a one-off normalization script (scripts/normalize-legacy-roles.sh) was run to rename project-prefixed bindings.
- Evidence chunking: evidence-generator split large audit fragments into 1MB chunks and generated a consolidated index file for ticket attachments.

SIEM export mapping (fields relied upon for automation):
- event_time (ISO8601)
- principal_id (user|service|bot)
- event_type (auth_success|auth_failure|role_grant|role_revoke|impersonation|token_create|token_exchange)
- resource (arn-like path for role or resource acted upon)
- action (read|write|admin|impersonate|deploy)
- actor_ip
- region
- request_id
- impersonator_id (optional, critical for delegated flows)
- session_id
Notes: 'impersonation' events must include impersonator_id and original_principal_id. If missing, evidence automation flags ticket for manual review.

Audit log schema suggestions (post-run):
- Make impersonator_id mandatory for token_exchange/impersonation events.
- Add derived_role_name field to role_grant/role_revoke events so downstream ETL can trace to RBAC v2 canonical names.
- Include policy_snapshot_id on role change events when the role change was driven by policy automation (helps distinguish human vs system grants).

Automation pipeline tweaks planned:
- evidence-generator: add resumable uploads and index manifest to avoid ticketing size limits. (Owner: Luca Chen, ETA: 2026-06-01)
- siem-forwarder: integrate a health-check that fails CI if TZ or localtime drift is detected; include backfill job to automatically reconcile gaps older than 24 hours. (Owner: Rina Gupta, ETA: 2026-06-10)
- rbac-normalizer: fold legacy binding patterns into canonical role labels during ingestion to prevent duplicate derived roles. (Owner: Priya Patel, ETA: 2026-05-20)

Exception handling notes:
- Exceptions that spanned >30 days need a documented mitigation plan in the ticket (compensating controls, monitoring, alternative access controls). We observed some exception requests without mitigation content; these were rejected by compliance.
- Automated reminder cadence: changed from 7/3/1 to 14/7/3 days for lower-risk groups to reduce churn.

Reviewer feedback (synthesized):
- Reviewers wanted a quick snapshot: top 3 recent activities in the last 30 days, last role change, and explicit list of resources the role can access. Evidence generator now surfaces the recent activity top-3 by event_type.
- Ticket UI: reviewers asked for a "show raw audit" toggle. We will propose a lightweight viewer that streams fragments rather than embeds entire logs.

Remediation backlog (short list):
- SEV-1: Add impersonator_id to token exchange events (security + infra) — JIRA-SC-4988.
- SEV-2: SIEM forwarder health-check and auto-backfill — JIRA-SC-4999.
- Medium: Evidence chunking + resumable uploads for large artifacts — JIRA-SC-5003.
- Low: Role derivation ruleset coverage for historical role_bindings — JIRA-SC-5011.

Action items (owners and ETA):
- Document permanent RBAC v2 normalization rules and ship to ingestion (Priya Patel, 2026-05-20).
- Implement evidence resumable manifest and test with ticketing sandbox (Luca Chen, 2026-06-01).
- Add impersonation field requirement to audit schema and roll enforcement to forwarders (Rina Gupta + Infra, 2026-05-18).
- Run a partial reconciliation pass for APAC logs for May 3–4 and certify backfill (SRE team, 2026-05-16).

Post-mortem notes for final report:
- Root cause summary: a small set of schema inconsistencies (impersonation fields, derived_role labels) combined with a deployment change (sidecar update) that caused temporary SIEM ingestion drift. No evidence of unauthorized access, but lineage proof for some delegated flows was incomplete.
- Customer and regulator impact: None reported; internal audit will note the missing lineage as a control gap and expect closure of SEV-1 by end of Q2.

Open questions and unresolved items:
- Should policy-driven grants include a signed policy_snapshot_id field at issuance time? (compliance leaning yes; engineering concerned about payload size)
- Do we archive raw full-audit fragments or only summarized indices by default? Cost vs fidelity tradeoff.

Notes to the reviewer:
- Attachments: sample ticket with full evidence (ticket-id: SEC-REC-2026-1247) and normalized role mapping export located in the infra repo PR.
- If you need raw logs for any principal, contact SRE (sre-support@redwood.com) and reference the ticket id above.

Appendix (quick commands used during run):
- normalize script: scripts/normalize-legacy-roles.sh --dry-run --apply
- evidence chunker test: python tools/evidence_chunker.py --input sample-audit.json --max-size 1048576
- siem backfill: infra/tools/siem-backfill --start 2026-05-03T00:00Z --end 2026-05-04T12:00Z --region apac

End of field notes.
